purpose: Pregabalin is used to treat nerve pain caused by conditions like diabetes, shingles, or spinal cord injury. It is also used to help control certain types of seizures and to treat fibromyalgia. Some doctors also prescribe it for anxiety disorders.
how_it_works: Your nerves sometimes send too many pain signals to your brain, which is what causes that burning or shooting pain. Pregabalin works by calming down those overactive nerve signals so they do not fire as strongly or as often. Think of it like turning down the volume on a radio that is playing too loud.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects are dizziness, drowsiness, and feeling unsteady on your feet. You may also notice blurry vision, dry mouth, swelling in your hands or feet, weight gain, or trouble concentrating. These often improve after your body gets used to the medication.
warnings: Do not stop taking this medication suddenly without talking to your doctor, as this can cause withdrawal symptoms like headache, nausea, or trouble sleeping. Pregabalin can make you feel very drowsy, so be careful driving or using heavy machinery. It may increase thoughts of depression or suicide in some people, so let your doctor know right away if you notice mood changes. Avoid alcohol while taking this medication. It is a controlled substance because some people may misuse it.
typical_dosing: Dosing is different for each person and depends on what it is being used for. A common starting dose is 75 mg taken twice a day, or 50 mg taken three times a day. Your doctor may slowly increase your dose over time to find the amount that works best for you. The usual maximum dose is 300 to 600 mg per day. Always take it exactly as your doctor tells you.
